# Best portable power stations for camping

The right pick depends on how much you need to run. Prices below come from the reviews and may have changed.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
The 250-500Wh class is the sweet spot for weight and simplicity, according to [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).

- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249, 288Wh, 8.3 lb): their top overall pick. Jackery's own site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so look for the Plus at retailers like Amazon.
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 286Wh, 600W AC): the better pick if you want more output, and it's expandable.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199, 288Wh): built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you get the version with an AC outlet, not the "DC" variant.
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179, 268Wh, 600W AC): the budget option.
- **Bluetti Elite 30 V2** (288Wh, 600W): [TechRadar's](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations) budget pick.

**Caveat:** [OutdoorGearLab's](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station) lab tests scored the Jackery 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low. Their recommendations lean toward bigger units, so these small ones are best if you only need to charge small electronics.

## Multi-day trips or running a cooler or fridge
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2**: OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It has 2,042Wh, 2,200W output, and weighs 39 lb. The list price is $1,499, but it's been found for under $900. It can't be expanded and isn't suited to electric burners or space heaters.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2**: OutdoorGearLab's best value pick. It's under $530 on sale and weighs 25 lb. Its fan is noisy and capacity is limited (890Wh measured).
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** ($1,079 on sale): [WIRED's](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/) camping pick. It has 1,536Wh, an IP65 rating, and weighs about 40 lb.
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**: TechRadar's camping pick, and PowerStationGearLab's pick for van life (~$799).
- **Bluetti AC180** ($499, 1,152Wh, 1,800W, ~35 lb): a mid-size option for weekend trips and tools. [Buy at Bluetti's official store](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180). This is an affiliate link, and the page lists code AFF5OFF for $24.95 off, which the site says it tested in Bluetti's cart. The checkout price is what counts.

## My recommendation
- **Most campers:** a 288Wh unit like the Jackery 300 Plus or Anker C300, if you just need to charge small devices.
- **Fridge, e-bike, or several days off-grid:** the Anker C1000 Gen 2 for value, or the Jackery 2000 v2 if you want more capacity.
- **Solar:** a matching folding solar panel makes longer trips easier. Jackery's own panels pair most easily with Jackery stations.

I only have direct purchase links for the Bluetti AC180. For the others, search the model name at Amazon, the brand's store, or the retailers listed in the reviews above. Check current price and model version before you buy.

If you tell me what you'll power and how many nights you camp, I can narrow this to one pick.
